request.system: Assess whether the hypothesis or expression uses or tests numbered claims. Return JSON only: {"uses_claim": true|false, "claim_ids": []}. Return one bare JSON object without Markdown fences or commentary. uses_claim must be a JSON boolean. claim_ids must be an array of integer claim numbers, never quoted strings; use an empty array when uses_claim is false.
request.prompt: {"claims": {"1": "**Findings after four submissions**", "2": "Three ideas failed.", "3": "Acceleration in average hours, persistence of rises in the stock rate, and a three-month shift between two flow rates each gave near-zero mean rank correlations.", "4": "Their t-statistics were below one, so all three failed our falsification rule.", "5": "One idea worked modestly.", "6": "Annual hourly-pay growth, standardized against each group's own three-year history, produced a positive rank correlation with a t-statistic just above two.", "7": "It was stronger in low-T periods.", "8": "Caveats: coverage dropped to about sixty percent because of the long history requirement, and the signal is highly persistent.", "9": "Pay-based signals deserve further robustness testing."}, "hypothesis": "Final robustness check, data-informed by submissions 2 and 4: if relative V03 rises over V02 genuinely predict outperformance, seasonally neutral year-over-year changes should also predict higher relative returns next month, in both T regimes.", "expression": "spread(yoy(V03),yoy(V02))"}
